dish: copper-griddled hot cake (cut in six) and house pudding
n: Junkissa American (純喫茶アメリカン)
w: Dōtonbori jun-kissa (roots 1946, at 1-7-4 Dōtonbori since 1950) with chandeliers, Italian red marble and a spiral staircase; Time Out calls it one of Osaka's most iconic kissaten, and Osaka Metro's OsakaMania and Kansai Walker feature its copper-griddled hot cake.

dish: Ōgonkai Ramen (golden freshwater-clam & chicken broth, light shoyu)
n: Naniwa Menjiro (なにわ 麺次郎)
address: 4-1-17 Namba, Chūō-ku, Osaka 542-0076 (inside Kintetsu Osaka-Namba Station — platform ticket needed)
w: Michelin Guide-listed ramen counter inside Kintetsu Osaka-Namba Station and a Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten 2025 pick; the clam-dashi Ōgonkai ramen is the signature, with Oigatsuo ramen as runner-up.

Hōzenji Yokochō's oldest restaurant (founded 1893), whose kantodaki Oda Sakunosuke wrote into Meoto Zenzai (1940); ranked #4 on TV Tokyo's Adomachi Tengoku Hōzenji Yokochō episode (12 Feb 2011), and Osaka's official tourism guide highlights its miso oden.

n: Creo-Ru Dōtonbori (たこ焼き くれおーる 道頓堀)
w: Big canal-side Dōtonbori takoyaki house (also okonomiyaki and kushikatsu); Time Out praises its faultless takoyaki and canal-view counter, and Osaka's official tourism Minami model course routes visitors here.

dish: hamburg steak with house demi-glace; two-egg omurice
w: Namba yōshoku house founded 1946 whose hamburg steak and omurice are unchanged since opening; Tabelog Yōshoku Hyakumeiten 2022, ranked #25 on TV Tokyo's Adomachi Tengoku Namba–Dōtonbori episode (2005), and in Kansai Walker's Naniwa yōshoku roundup.

n: Okonomiyaki Yukari Sennichimae (ゆかり 千日前店)
w: Sennichimae branch of the Osaka okonomiyaki house credited with handing down the 'mixed' Osaka style; recommended in OSAKA-INFO's Japan Konamon Association konamon guide and in SAVOR JAPAN's 15 best okonomiyaki in Osaka.

dish: omakase kushiage (kushikatsu) course paired with wine
address: Kuromon Market arcade, Nipponbashi, Chūō-ku, Osaka
w: Fine-dining kushiage counter inside the Kuromon Market arcade; the Michelin Guide's kushikatsu feature notes it won a Michelin star in 2009 for elevating kushikatsu with premium ingredients and wine, and SAVOR JAPAN's Minami picks list it.
